# The Wristband: how music festivals work, everywhere

> A cited, independent field guide to music festivals: history, who owns them, where the money goes, how lineups are booked and sold, building the site, crowd safety, wristbands and cashless, camping, impact and the global season, plus a festival finder.

A cited field guide (311 sources, about 34,404 words) to how music festivals work, everywhere: the history of the music festival, who owns the big festivals, where the money goes, how lineups are booked and billed, how festivals sell out, building the site, crowd safety and heat, wristbands and cashless payment, camping and transport, waste and local impact, the global festival season, and New England from Newport to Boston Calling, plus a festival finder. Independent; not affiliated with any festival.

## Key facts
- How do festival RFID wristbands work? The chip in the band carries a unique ID number, not your personal details, and readers look it up in the festival's database at gates and bars. NFC chips read at about 4 cm for payments, and UHF chips read at about 1-6 m for fast gate entry, according to a 2026 vendor guide.
- How do I get a refund of my cashless festival balance? Request it online after the festival, inside the published window if there is one. Fees in 2025-2026 examples ran from 0.50 euros at splash! to 3.50 euros at Dour, and Dour says credit not claimed by its deadline is lost.
- How many toilets do you need per person at a festival? UK council guidance for events open six hours or more starts at 1 toilet per 100 women and 1 toilet per 500 men plus 1 urinal per 150 men. Shorter events start at 1 per 150 women and 1 per 600 men plus 1 urinal per 175.
- When is festival season in Europe? Europe's peak runs from June to August, with July the most crowded month. In 2025 Exit, Mad Cool, FIB and Tomorrowland all ran in July, and Awakenings ran in July 2026.
- What is an early bird festival ticket? It is the cheapest tier, sold first in limited numbers, and the price steps up once it sells out. Lollapalooza's 2013 early-bird three-day passes were $200; the next tier was $235.
- Does Glastonbury make a profit? Yes. Glastonbury reported revenue of £68.4 million and profit of £5.9 million for 2024, per Companies House filings reported by DJ Mag, after record losses in 2020 and 2021.
- How much does it cost to go to a music festival? One financial planner estimated $800 to $3,000 for a US festival trip in 2024, including ticket, travel, lodging and food. A 2024 Opinium poll found 65% of UK adults think festivals are becoming too expensive.
- Is Boston Calling coming back in 2027? Possibly, but it is not confirmed. There was no Boston Calling in 2026, and in June 2025 organizers announced a return for June 4-6, 2027, but as of October 2026 they had not confirmed that edition and Axios Boston reported the festival's future "in doubt" with organizers silent.
